head: 203e74c
summary: Fixed shared governed-query validation/refusal metadata, anonymous HTTP attribution and finding-history timestamp rendering. Added repeatable isolated API/gateway replay and a separate read-only policy audit. Strict build, format and 1551 fast tests pass; 15 Python policy/setup tests pass. Both complete replays ran repeatedly: API 1514 steps/2311 raw fields; gateway 255/523. Final ordered failure lists exactly reproduce the post-fix run. Local percentage board: framework 17/17, reads 406/414, claims 295/316, drafts 313/323, AI 27/27, gateway 236/255. All named percentage targets pass, but unconditional convergence stops at the inherited framework waiver cap: 9/17, 52.94%, exceeds 25%. HALT and reports explain the policy conflict; no threshold or comparison was weakened and no new waiver added. Head identifies the tested implementation/tooling commit; the following documentation commit records this status. Local commits only; no live systems or owned hosts left running.

deviations.what: The reported standalone gateway composition failure did not reproduce on the supplied merged branch.
deviations.why: The ordinary gateway already references and composes application/runtime services in-process. Proved repeatability and corrected stale documentation rather than add duplicate registrations or a second API listener.

deviations.what: The final board is explicitly a local policy audit, not an external conductor result.
deviations.why: Raw semantic replay is unchanged. The historical diagnostic predates the approved F-18 exception and treats digits in native HTML as numeric figures. The new read-only audit documents exact current policy application and exposes waiver shares separately.

deviations.what: Stopped under the Stage-4 gate/policy rule despite passing all named percentage targets.
deviations.why: Framework retains 9/17 waived cases, above the inherited 25% cap. W2 disclosed the same conflict. Reproducing framework markup or unsafe CORS solely to reduce the share would violate the task; no cap or comparison was changed.

deviations.what: Used the fixed session-named improvements/integrate-W3.json, intentionally empty.
deviations.why: Production repairs restore recorded intended behavior and need no deliberate-difference waiver. A second converge-w3 register would duplicate ownership and contradict the fixed finish rule.

findings: Initial merged strict build, format and all 1545 fast tests already passed; no stale test, duplicate registration or dependency conflict reproduced.
The supplied gateway 83/255 summary is not the measured baseline on the correct two hosts. Fresh local gateway baseline is 233/255 under documented policy; after real repairs it is 236/255.

Empty employee queries incorrectly hit raw-person authorization before semantic validation; distinct unknown/blocked/non-category columns also needed separate refusals and column metadata. Four new cases prove no invalid question reaches the provider.
Anonymous local HTTP writes were misattributed as system. Shared defaults now say anonymous while authenticated-person attribution and explicit engine/package defaults are unchanged.
Finding history leaked provider timestamp padding. Canonical instant hydration preserves meaningful microseconds without changing stored timestamps or audit durability.
Final raw reports contain 2834 differing fields across 1769 steps; they are not zero-difference replay passes. The local policy audit retains all unresolved fields and source-report hashes.
Framework waiver cases are four native documentation exchanges, four readiness descriptions and one safer CORS exchange. Documentation plus CORS alone is 5/17, already above the inherited cap.

Gateway remains 19 failed cases/49 fields: two person-lane refusals/16 fields, two governed catalogues/17 fields, fifteen genuine identity cases/16 fields. No changed tool figure or missing fact was waived.

Python claim previews allocate temporary identities; pure .NET previews do not. Later confirmations, correlations and package identities diverge. No dummy draws or response-ID rewriting were introduced.
The typed governed-query port supports eight warehouse datasets; three source-data datasets remain unavailable. Their catalogue count differences are visible and unwaived.

Remaining API backlog is reads 8 cases/148 fields, claims 21/100 and drafts 10/19; these include monetary-string scale, IDs, storage bounds, degraded availability and stored program/base-year semantics.
M-01 ingestion precedence and first-program credit pricing remain figure-sensitive inherited behavior. Row-count/max-modified source fingerprints are observations, not immutable snapshots.
All final ordered failure lists exactly equal the previous post-fix complete run. The actual host executable processes were checked absent after runner cleanup.
open_questions: How should the inherited framework waiver cap account for registered native documentation, safer CORS and truthful readiness without requiring forbidden framework-artifact emulation?
How should the owner reconcile fixed-tool person-lane privacy with recorded valid-request authorization outcomes?

needs_human.item: Resolve the inherited framework waiver accounting/cap policy.
needs_human.why: Immediate convergence blocker: framework percentage is 100%, but 9/17 cases are waived (52.94%) against the inherited 25% limit. This session neither relaxes the cap nor assumes the W2 conductor's silence changed it.

needs_human.item: Reconcile person-derived fixed-tool facts with valid-request authorization preservation.
needs_human.why: Two MCP Cowork calls return employee_level_not_allowed where Python returned unmarked person-derived facts. Existing safer lane checks remain unchanged; missing facts and authorization differences remain unwaived.

needs_human.item: Resolve genuine deterministic identity histories without dummy allocations.
needs_human.why: Pure previews omit Python's throwaway claim IDs, while durable audits have their own real allocations. Later confirmation, correlation, run, override and artifact identities remain visible; removing durability or spending dummy IDs is prohibited.

needs_human.item: Choose contractual native money-string scale and valid long-text storage behavior.
needs_human.why: Native DECIMAL4 strings differ from recorded shorter strings; some valid long strings exceed storage bounds. No float conversion, truncation or changed-figure waiver is acceptable.

needs_human.item: Complete source-data governed-query and inherited provider/fiscal proofs.
needs_human.why: Raw payroll, location and pay-code query bindings, safe cross-year distinct-person suppression, native monetary AVG, zero-worksite SQL semantics, strict leap-day fiscal behavior and live artifact publication remain unproved or incomplete.

needs_human.item: Approve any figure-affecting M-01 or first-program pricing correction.
needs_human.why: M-01 contradicts year-pack precedence, but both it and first-program multi-program pricing affect figures and are deliberately preserved pending owner reconciliation.

needs_human.item: Accept the source-version observation limit or choose a stronger source.
needs_human.why: Row count plus maximum modified timestamp misses count/max-preserving edits and is not an immutable source snapshot.

needs_human.item: Define cross-replica idempotency, uncertain-write recovery and workflow retention.
needs_human.why: Existing host-local leases and atomic same-confirmation consume do not prove global different-confirmation key reservation; no agreed result-recovery endpoint or process/replica durability protocol exists.

needs_human.item: Prove trusted orchestrator ingress/employer binding in W4.
needs_human.why: Platform-injected original-subject headers need authenticated ingress that strips spoofable assertions. No live identity, deployment grants or private payroll access was authorized here.

needs_human.item: Retain remaining orchestrator configuration and coverage decisions.
needs_human.why: Optional safety-control off-switches remain explicitly refused; complete model-scripted cross-surface golden matrices, live retrieval/network probes and the previously unverified named guarantees remain outside this hermetic convergence evidence.
